notes: The 1968 volume of the Recreation and Park Commission. Curated: design approvals and architects' agreements, the Portsmouth Square bridge, a pool dedication.

coverage.remaining: Routine items not curated. Not placed: Ward's sketch for a Senior Center on the Leroy Vane bequest at Kennedy Drive, 8th Avenue and Fulton (Mar 14; site undecided); the Chovin sculpture and fountains model for the Palace of Fine Arts lagoon (Jan 25); Hans Gerson's Palace of Fine Arts display lighting plans (Nov 14).
coverage.note: Dated by meeting openers (Feb 21 was a Wednesday meeting). Curated list F1968.py.

findings.address_as_written: Pedestrian bridge between the Chinese Cultural Center and Portsmouth Square
findings.description: After a hearing at which some speakers objected to its effect on the children's play area, the Recreation and Park Commission approved in principle the Redevelopment Agency's plan for a pedestrian bridge over Kearny Street from the Chinese Cultural Center to Portsmouth Square, on condition that the developer, Justice Enterprises, move the children's area at its own cost; the bridge, presented in September by the architect Clement Chen, Jr., was part of a building with a 27-story hotel and the Chinese Cultural and Trade Center.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, November 14, 1968
